KNOWLEDGE AND AWARENESS OF THE GUIDELINES CONCERNING REPUBLIC ACT NO.
10863 BALIKBAYAN BOXES OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
Angelie Mae A. Abello, Margaret Ann A. Adato, Farrah T. Alaras, Marjorie O.
Alipan, Anthony S. Alvares, Ediric D. Gadia, Merlin De Gracia.
Gordon College, Olongapo City, Philippines
Abstract: The fact that overseas Filipino workers are considered our modern
heroes today is indisputable. From the remittances they send to their families
to the Balikbayan boxes filled with love, suffering, and sacrifices that they send
home, OFWs never cease to assist their families. The primary purpose of this
study was to determine whether Overseas Filipino Workers are well
knowledgeable and aware of the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863
Balikbayan Boxes. The researchers used a quantitative study, particularly
descriptive survey research design to collect OFWs' profiles and investigate
their knowledge and awareness of guidelines for sending balikbayan boxes. A
random sampling method was used to select 130 respondents, all of whom are
OFWs who have or have not previously sent a Balikbayan box. Survey
questionnaires were used to assess the knowledge and awareness of OFWs on
the Guidelines Concerning Republic Act No. 10863 Balikbayan Boxes. Data
were analyzed using frequency distribution, percentage, weighted mean,
descriptive rating, t-test, and analysis of variance. According to the result of
the study, the majority of the OFW respondents are moderately aware, and
there is no statistically significant difference between the knowledge and
awareness of OFWs on the Guidelines Concerning Republic Act No. 10863
Balikbayan Boxes when grouped according to their profile variables.
Keywords: Overseas Filipino Workers, balikbayan box, knowledge, awareness,
Republic Act No. 10863

31 | Pa ge
1. INTRODUCTION
Sending balikbayan boxes has become a part of Filipino tradition as the
number of Filipinos living abroad rises steadily. Overseas Filipino Workers still
heavily practice the tradition of sending these boxes to the Philippines, which
dates back to the 1970s. The balikbayan box became popular circa the 1980s in
the United States due to the influx of overseas Filipino workers in the country.
According to Shyong (2018), the first freight forwarder to offer balikbayan box
services was Rico Nunga, who started REN International in Los Angeles,
California, in 1981. Prior to then-President Cory Aquino’s Executive Order No.
206, balikbayan boxes were subject to taxes; however, it was later declared
duty- and tax-free on non-commercial products worth up to P10,000. This is a
direct result of the hardships and laborious work put in by OFWs and their
favorable impact on the Philippine economy.
Since then, balikbayan boxes and Filipino overseas have both become a
representation of mobility and success.
Silk (2004) stated that items in the Balikbayan boxes not only contribute a
big help to the migrant’s family members but rather it also signifies that the
migrant has achieved the “better life” that they always wanted. It is also
interesting to see how these migrants prepared and packaged the items they
would send home. They can receive the best products and can also save money
by selecting the right retailer and items to add. One strategy for gathering the
items in balikbayan boxes is to travel outside of the city to shop for various
items that are on sale or at a discount. Another example of a method for
collecting items for the Balikbayan box is collecting old clothes, money, or even
electronic equipment given to the migrants by their employers or colleagues.
Such an arrangement works quite well people are willing to give something to
others living in a distant country because it fits into the logic of helping that
characterizes Western aid and development.
On the other hand, Ingles (2011) described the story of an Overseas Filipino
Workers toiling away in some obscure part of the world to pay for sibling’s
education or to fund a relative’s new business venture is all too familiar. OFWs
send balikbayan boxes and remit so much money as an expression of love to the
people left back home. This kind of generosity is not uncommon in modern
Filipino households. A balikbayan box is a symbol of sacrifice, too. All too
often, sending a balikbayan box filled to the brim means working extra hours or
using a credit card to afford everyone’s bilins. While most OFWs generally earn
substantial income, it doesn’t necessarily mean that they are not struggling
financially.
Section 2 of the Republic Act. No. 6768 (1989) states that the term
"balikbayan" refers to a Filipino citizen who has been continuously absent from
the Philippines for at least one (1) year, a Filipino overseas worker, or a former
Filipino citizen and his family, as defined herein, who was naturalized in a
foreign country and comes or returns to the Philippines.
Lawless (2004) in his study revealed that in 1973, the Philippine
Government under then-President Ferdinand Marcos began to specifically
encourage Filipino Americans to visit their family hometowns in the
Philippines. Individuals who did so became known as balikbayan, from the
Tagalog words balik, "to return", and bayan, "town/settlement". As part of this
program, customs procedures were eased for these travelers.

32 | Pa ge
As stated on the website of the Philippine Statistics Authority (2022) the
number of Filipinos who worked abroad during the period of April to September
2021 was estimated at 1.83 million and according to the Door-to-Door
Consolidated Association of the Philippines, 400,000 balikbayan boxes arrive
in the Philippines monthly.
Republic Act No. 10863, otherwise known as the Customs Modernization
and Tariff Act (CMTA) was signed into law on 30 May 2016. It was signed by
then President Noynoy Aquino thereby increasing the tax ceiling to up to
P150,000. This Act mandates that sending of balikbayan boxes by Qualified
Filipinos While Abroad (QFWA) to their families and relatives is exempt from
payment of duties and taxes up to three (3) times and not exceeding P150,000
in a calendar year. The purpose of section 800 (g) of Republic Act No. 10863,
titled Conditionally Tax And/or Duty-Exempt Importation, is to provide
guidelines to all qualified Filipinos abroad who are or will be sending boxes to
their families. Every sender of balikbayan boxes must be aware of the
conditions that must be met when sending the boxes containing their hard work
and love. Every person must have some knowledge of the law; otherwise, it
would be exceedingly difficult for everyone to handle a number of common
issues, such as consumer protection, societal protection of fundamental rights,
and others.
Customs Memorandum Order (CMO) No. 27-2015 provided that each
Balikbayan box sent by Overseas Filipino workers must go through an x-ray
process to determine what is inside, and every box will undergo a document
review to determine if all legal requirements have been complied with. In the
XIP image analysis, the inspector will "identify balikbayan box(es) with
possible violation and recommend the issuance of an alert order" if the shipment
is tagged "suspect" after x-ray scanning. Those boxes will then be subjected to
a 100% physical examination by a Bureau of Customs examiner in front of the
apprehending officers, freight forwarder/consolidator, representatives of the
Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), and/or designated officer
of an OFW association. On the other hand, any balikbayan boxes discovered to
be in compliance will be segregated and provisionally released to allow its
continuous processing. A tax exemption policy enables several regulations to
be enforced in packages that travel between the Philippines and the nations
where Filipinos are employed. Many studies have looked at the process and
challenges faced by Overseas Filipino workers in packing their balikbayan
boxes. However, there has not been a lot of attention given to the knowledge
and awareness of Overseas Filipino Workers in relation to Republic Act 10863
(g). That is what this study was designed to answer and investigate. Overseas
Filipino workers may be numerous, but ensuring and locating them was one of
the gaps encountered by the researchers. To ensure that the respondents are
OFWs, the majority of them are relatives of the researchers, and some are
friends of friends who work overseas of the researchers' families. Theories
regarding knowledge and awareness related to the topic of the research were
difficult to find. The researchers attempted a variety of theories, but the majority
were rejected since there was no proof that they were useful or related to the
research. On the other hand, the researchers use the Republic Act 10863 (g) as
their framework which is more applicable to the study.
With the stated information and situations, this study's main objective is to
assess the knowledge and awareness of the guidelines concerning Republic Act
No. 10863 Balikbayan Boxes of Overseas Filipino Workers. The Oxford

33 | Pa ge
Dictionary defines awareness as the quality or state of being aware,
consciousness; (also) the condition of being aware (of something or that
something is), and knowledge as the fact of knowing or being acquainted with
a thing, person, etc.; acquaintance; familiarity gained by experience. This
proposed study attempted to determine and evaluate how knowledgeable and
aware OFWs really are about the guidelines stated in Section 800(g) of the
CMTA which are implemented by the Bureau of Customs regarding balikbayan
boxes. It also aimed to propose a plan of action and recommendations to lessen
the problem.
The results of this study could be extremely significant and beneficial
specifically to the following: Overseas Filipino Workers. The study will provide
them with the dos and don’ts with regard to sending these boxes. The
information discussed in this study will lead them to know what the policies
imposed by the Bureau specifically in Section 800 of the CMTA, the different
types of goods that can only be sent home, as well as those classified as
prohibited goods, and the privileges they can enjoy. Bureau of Customs. The
results of this study will help strengthen their services for the welfare, security,
and benefits of the OFWs. Bachelor of Science in Customs Administration
(BSCA) students. As future licensed customs brokers or customs officers,
BSCA students will also benefit from this study as it will provide them with a
background on the guidelines that the Bureau of Customs implements,
specifically with regard to the balikbayan boxes. Future Researchers. This will
also be useful to future and aspiring researchers to plan and create pertinent
results for their studies similar to this current study.
2. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
2.1 Research Design
The study determined the level of knowledge and awareness of OFWs on the
guidelines about Republic Act No. 10863 Balikbayan Boxes. To achieve this
purpose, the researchers used a quantitative study, particularly descriptive,
survey research design to collect OFWs' profiles and investigate their
knowledge and awareness on guidelines of sending balikbayan boxes. As
indicated by Siedlecki (2020), descriptive quantitative study is used to describe
individuals, events, and conditions of the subject by studying them as they are
in nature without any manipulation. The descriptive research design focuses on
the present condition and the purpose is to uncover new truths. By the use of
descriptive, survey research design, researchers gathered data to answer
questions with regard to the topic. The study was also made by the use of a
questionnaire as an instrument for data gathering.
2.2. Research Instrument
The survey form's questions were all based on Republic Act No. 10863, but
modified in order to achieve the objective of the study. As a result, the
researchers employed an adapted modified questionnaire using Google forms
as their research instrument. The questionnaire contains contents of Sec.800 (g)
of Republic Act No. 10863 which is about the conditionally tax/and or duty-
free importation of balikbayan boxes. Close-ended questions were used to
easily gather the information needed for the research. The aim of the survey
questionnaire is to determine the level of knowledge and awareness of the

34 | Pa ge
guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863 Balikbayan Boxes of Overseas
Filipino Workers. To get the appropriate data needed the researchers made a
three (3) parts survey questionnaire as the main data gathering instrument.
Part 1 was made by the researchers to determine the profile of the
respondents; age, sex, country of work, number of years abroad, province in the
Philippines and number of times send a balikbayan box.
Part 2 questionnaire tool consists of 6 questions that will be used to
determine the level of awareness of the respondents. The data gathering
instrument was structured on a scale ranging from 1-4. Where in (4) is Highly
aware, (3) is Moderately aware, (2) is Slightly aware, and (1) is not aware.
Part 3 questionnaire tool also consists of 6 questions that will be used to
determine the level of knowledge of the respondents. The data gathering
instrument was structured on a scale ranging from 1-4. Where (4) is Highly
knowledgeable, (3) is Moderately knowledgeable, (2) is Slightly
knowledgeable, and (1) is not knowledgeable.
2.3 Treatment of Data
The data gathered were tabulated, organized and processed through
Microsoft Excel (2019) and Statistical Package for Social Sciences version 20
(SPSS v.20). The following statistical procedures were utilized:
1. Frequency and Percentage Distribution were used to categorize the profile
of the respondent in terms of age, sex, country of work, number of years abroad,
region in the Philippines, and number of times send a Balikbayan Box.
2. Weighted Mean was used to describe the level of Knowledge and
Awareness of the respondents regarding the guidelines concerning Republic
Act No. 10863 Balikbayan Boxes of Overseas Filipino Workers.
3. T- test and (ANOVA) Analysis of Variance these were used to test
the significant differences on the level of Knowledge and Awareness of the
respondents regarding the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863
Balikbayan Boxes of Overseas Filipino Workers when grouped according to
profile variables. The level of significance used is 0.05.
3. Presentation, Analysis And Interpretation Of Data
This section presents the findings, analysis and interpretation given in
relation to the problem being investigated. It includes the profile of the
respondents, level of knowledge and awareness about balikbayan box, and
differences between the variables.

Duty- and tax-free privileges are granted to certain people. Section 800 of
the CMTA provides duty- and tax-free privileges to returning Filipino residents,
who have stayed in a foreign country for a period of at least six months; overseas
Filipino workers (OFWs) who hold valid passports and working in a foreign
country under employment contracts; and overseas Filipinos who now reside or
are citizens of other countries and are coming to resettle in the Philippines.
Balikbayans are also entitled to such privileges. Aside from OFWs and overseas
Filipinos, balikbayans include “Filipino citizens who have been continuously
out of the Philippines for a period of at least one year”.

Filipinos who work and reside in other countries generally fill the
Balikbayan boxes throughout the year and send them to their families a few
months before the Christmas or New Year season, as well as other significant
holidays. The increase begins in September, which marks the beginning of the
Christmas season for many Filipinos. The majority of these balikbayan boxes
arriving at the Port of Manila are from Asian countries, with Canada and the
United States following closely behind (Tristram, 2023).

CONCLUSION
Based on the findings generated from the study, the following conclusions
were hereby drawn:
1. The majority of the respondents were aged 31-40 years old and
primarily were females and working in China (Hong Kong) for
about 0-5 years abroad and from Region III and had sent Balikbayan
Boxes below 10 times.

52 | Pa ge
2. The result exhibited that the respondents were moderately
knowledgeable in terms of their level of knowledge of the guidelines
concerning Republic Act No. 10863 section 800 (g).
3. From the study, it was also concluded that the respondents were
moderately aware in terms of their level of awareness being described
in terms of the contents of Republic Act No. 10863 section 800 (g).
4. Awareness of Overseas Filipino Workers in terms of age was
found to be significant. Similarly, knowledge of OFWs in terms of country
of work, the region in the Philippines, and the number of times sent a
Balikbayan Box was also found to be significant. The rest of the
variables affirm the null hypothesis that there is no significant
difference between the knowledge and awareness of the respondents
when grouped according to profile variables.
5. To help develop and improve the knowledge and awareness of the
OFWs of the various guidelines about Republic Act No. 10863, section
800 (g) Balikbayan Boxes, an infographic is made containing essential
information about how to send a balikbayan box, the requirements
needed, the restricted and prohibited goods, and the privilege that
OFWs may avail in sending balikbayan boxes. Furthermore, aside
from an infographic, a plan of action is hereby proposed to
disseminate both knowledge & awareness regarding Republic Act No.
10863, 800 (g). The specific activity is to disseminate essential tools that
will help respondents become more knowledgeable and aware by
intensifying social media use through posting in OFW social media
groups and sending messages via Messenger, Viber, or any social
media platforms available.
RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the findings and conclusions of the following
recommendations are provided to enhance the Knowledge and Awareness of
the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863 balikbayan boxes of
Overseas Filipino Workers.
1. Full coordination among the Shipping Companies and Overseas
Filipino Workers and the Bureau of Customs engaging in the
transaction may be watched to ensure the operation's efficiency.
2. The Bureau of Customs may provide an effective dissemination of
information about the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863
balikbayan box to Overseas Filipino Workers.
3. All Overseas Filipino Workers may have an easy access to a
portal/site that allows them to obtain all of the necessary information when
sending a balikbayan box to their loved ones.
4. The Bureau of Customs may develop adequate communication
with all Overseas Filipino Workers worldwide, expressing their
ideas and feedback for precise quality outcomes.
5. For future researchers to do more exploring regarding the topic to
further enhance the validity and reliability of the study. Also, to explore the
shortcomings and problem of the study to make it more adaptable.

53 | Pa ge

EMPLOYABILITY OF BS CUSTOMS ADMINISTRATION GRADUATES OF GORDON COLLEGE
YEAR 2018-2022
Mary Francine V. Agana, Warren Nikko M. Arenga, Charles Jesper B.
Bantican, Andrie Maurice C. Bacani, Ivan Pineda (+), Ediric D. Gadia, Patricia
Anne Paras.
Gordon College, Olongapo City, Philippines
Abstract: Tracer studies have been employed as a monitoring tool for students'
transition from academic life to professional life. It attempts to follow
graduates' professional progress in relation to the value of the knowledge and
training they received from the college. To determine which courses and
programs have aided the student in achieving the anticipated career path after
graduation, it also provides an assessment of the curriculum design for each of
the relevant courses and programs. This quantitative-descriptive study aimed
to determine the graduates' employability for the Bachelor of Science in
Customs Administration from 2018–2022. This study utilized the descriptive
method of research, in which a total of one hundred four graduates
participated. Data were gathered using the institutional instrument for the
tracer study. Findings revealed that the majority of the graduates secured a job
within a month, with regular status, and are presently employed as
professionals in logistics companies.
Keywords: BSCA graduates, employability, school-related factors, tracer
study.

56 | Pa ge
1. INTRODUCTION
Nowadays, graduates are faced with a challenge of seeking for employment
after graduation. Refozar & Del Mundo (2013) emphasized on their study that
there seem to have a wide gap between number of graduates and absorption
rates. And the usual cause, as claimed, is the apparent weak preparation of
graduates with job requirements of the government and private organizations.
The truth of the matter is that jobs are available, but it seems that very few
qualify for the available jobs. One of the problems of students in getting
employed after graduation is meeting the job requirements that an organization
requires of applicants for a job. However, job requirements vary from company
to company for it has its own set of criteria in human resource procurement and
development. It is therefore the concern of every higher education institution to
provide its students with pre-employment preparations to getting jobs. Such
preparations must be research-based to be sure that the training given to students
would prepare them for employment not only in the provincial or local labor
market, but more importantly, in national and later on in international labor
markets.
The difficulty of finding work after graduation is something that graduates
must overcome. They are searching for the best job opening available. The
intense competition on the labor market and graduates' lack of employability
skills make it difficult for them to find work. According to the Philippine Star
(2017), just one in three college graduates in the nation are "employable," which
indicates that 65 percent of Filipino graduates lack the education and experience
necessary to be qualified for the jobs they are looking for. High unemployment
rates are associated with both economic inefficiency and social instability,
according to Aspiring Minds.
It has been said that the Philippines formal education has been lacking in
producing productive graduates. This goes to say that there is really a need for
students to be trained to become globally competitive, fully equipped with the
proper work values, in order to make a big difference in the world of work. On
their part, they suggested four criteria for evaluating training, such as the reaction
level, the learning level, or how well they learned and retained what they learned,
the behavioral level, and the results level, or the final results obtained from the
training (Refozar and Del Mundo, 2013).
The graduate tracer research offers useful details regarding what happens to
our recent graduates when they enter the workforce. Finding out how well our
institution's training prepares students for their job life as a whole and the extent
to which knowledge, communication, and other abilities have been acquired are
equally essential. The results of this tracer research can also be used as a basis
for future planning activities by offering important data for assessing an
institution's educational and training outcomes (Ramirez et al., 2021).
Numerous studies have examined the employability of graduates from
various courses of graduate track studies based on various research.
Nevertheless, the employability of graduates in customs administration has only
been studied once, and that study focused solely on graduates from a specific
university (Casa et al., 2022). In this study, the researchers intended to find out
the present employment status of Gordon College Bachelor of Science in

57 | Pa ge
Customs Administration graduates. The contribution or benefit of this study is
that it will be one of the bases for the students inside and outside of the school
to inspire them to enroll and continue their college course at Gordon College,
especially if they feel that their path for a career is in customs administration.
Additionally, the researchers, who are enrolled in the same program as the
respondents, believe that this study is important since it will provide
information about the respondents' employability in the future. Finally, this
study will aid future researchers by providing a foundation for their research,
which may eventually relate to the subject or area of interest of this study.
2. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
2.1 Research Design
This study utilizes quantitative research using descriptive method. The
primary goal of the study is to evaluate the employability of BSCA graduates
of Gordon College. The primary goal of the study is to evaluate the
employability of BSCA graduates of Gordon College. Calderon (2006) defined
descriptive research as a purposeful process of gathering, analyzing, classifying,
and tabulating data about prevailing conditions, practices, processes, trends, and
cause-effect relationships and then making adequate and accurate
interpretations about such data with or without or sometimes with minimal aid
of statistical methods. This method is relatively suitable for the study because
it describes the present status of the alumni.
2.2 Research Instrument
The researchers used a survey questionnaire to gather the necessary data
for this study. The questionnaire used is from the Commission on Higher
Education (CHED). The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has
verified the validity and reliability of our survey questionnaire, which has been
in use since its developed by CHED. The questionnaire consists of four main
sections: the respondents' general profile, educational background, post-college
programs, and employment information.
2.3 Treatment of Data
In this study, the data were analyzed and interpreted using the percentage
and frequency distribution methods. This was used to calculate the percentage
distribution and frequency counts of the respondents' personally related
variables. Percentage were used by the researcher to convert the numerical data
gathered from the questionnaire. The descriptive statistic used frequency and
percentage. These things would be explained further in the following:
a. Frequency – pertains to the number of respondents that have the same answer
in a specific question.
b. Percentage – used to determine the ratio of respondents that have the same
answers as the general number of respondents.

Based from the respondents' profiles, the majority are single, most are men, a
substantial number are from region 3, almost all are from Olongapo City, and a
significant proportion live in the city.

RESPONDENTS
The respondents' employment profile indicates that a significant percentage are
employed, with most citing reasons for unemployment as not actively seeking
jobs or lacking job opportunities, the majority holding regular or permanent
positions, a large proportion working as professionals, the vast majority
employed locally, over half securing their first jobs through recommendations,
a substantial portion landing their first jobs in less than a month, and the
majority finding their first jobs relevant to their college curriculum.

CHALLENGES ENCOUNTERED AND COPING STRATEGIES OF CUSTOMS BROKER
PRACTICING AT SOME PORT
Rhea Jane A. Altares, Maricel A. Agan, Yvonne Q. Anulao, Juliene Gwyneth
J. Atazar, Ian P. Balingit, Ediric D. Gadia, Sherinne Angel Malong.
Gordon College, Olongapo City, Philippines
Abstract: The study aims to determine the relationship between challenges
encountered and coping strategies of Customs Brokers practicing in a certain
port located in Olongapo City, Philippines. The proponents decided to use a
mixed method as research design to achieve the study’s primary aim. The study
also utilized a purposive sample technique to gathered 40 respondents to
answer the survey questionnaires-via Google form. The proponents adopted
and modified an instrument in order to fit with the aims of the study and
subjected it to validity and reliability test. The study determined the challenges
and coping strategies using descriptive and inferential statistics with the help
of SPSS 23. Result shows that slow computer systems and computer system
breakdown were the primary challenges encountered by the practitioners. On
the other hand, customs broker seeks assistance from fellow customs broker
was the most effective and used coping strategy among the respondents. Finally,
the study also revealed a weak positive correlation between the challenges
encountered and the respondents’ coping strategies. In conclusion, there was a
weak relationship between the challenges encountered and the coping
strategies of the respondents. The researchers provided some recommendations
at the end of the study.
Keywords: Customs brokerage, Bureau of Customs, Freight forwarding, Import
and export, Work challenges, Coping strategies

69 | Pa ge
1. INTRODUCTION
Economic growth nowadays is primarily dependent on the dynamics of
international trade, which is where customs brokerage plays an important role.
Without it, importers and exporters who lack the time and knowledge of
customs rules and regulations would be unable to conduct business effectively.
The Philippine economy includes a significant percentage of the customs
brokerage sector. Communication between the government, importers, and
exporters is facilitated by it. A customs broker must hold a valid license in order
to deal with the Bureau of Customs on behalf of an importer or exporter.
Customs brokerage services provided in the Philippines include consultation,
preparation of import and export customs documentation, declaration and
payment of customs duties and taxes, and processing of import and export
entries (Republic Act No. 9280).
To fulfill the needs of international trade, customs brokerage services are
necessary due to the many requests from numerous clients. Customs brokers
find it challenging to steer clear of challenges when doing their duties, which
might result in customer resentment and shipment delays. Problems can also
occur as a result of client negligence, such as failing to submit or complete
necessary documents, unanticipated events like natural disasters and accidents
that delay the delivery of goods, and, occasionally, as a result of
misunderstandings and giving customs brokers too little time to complete their
work (Ermita et. al., 2016).
Customs brokers also face the challenge of meeting compliance and service
obligations while maintaining the costs required to deliver value to the market.
Global security concerns, economic uncertainty, and varying Customs and other
government agency approaches and processes represent true professional
challenges, as stated by Lorenze (2016).
In the study of Cuevas et al. (2018), the three most frequent issues customs
brokers run into are delays, damaged goods, and customs clearance. Customs
brokers also have a difficult time importing and exporting goods because they
must abide by the laws and regulations. They deal with a lot of uncertainty,
including current macrotrends. Additionally, they experience problems with
client negligence, communication with the importer, and document submission
problems (Lenari, 2013).
On the other hand, as stated by Sambayan (2014), the customs brokers
concurred that they have issues with incomplete documents, pending office
transactions, and low volumes of transactions. If left unattended, the challenges
they face could turn into a major issue for the entire process.
The transaction between the exporter or importer, customs broker, and
government agencies involved in keeping their goods moving through customs
and across borders, which is one of our country's significant sources of income,
would be impacted by the aforementioned problems. The researchers made the
decision to conduct this study as a result in order to offer solutions to the issues
they had identified.
The researchers chose to look into the challenges encountered and coping
mechanisms used by customs brokers practicing at the Port of Subic.
According to Republic Act No. 9280 otherwise known as the “Customs
Brokers Act of 2004”, licensed customs brokers are experts who focus on
offering services to importers and exporters. An importer or exporter engages a

70 | Pa ge
customs broker to represent him or her with the Bureau of Customs throughout
the process. Customs brokers assist clients with the preparation of necessary
documentation and/or electronic submissions, computation and payment of
taxes, duties, and excises, as well as facilitating interaction between importers
and exporters and governmental agencies.
The challenges raised by the customs brokers with whom the researchers
spoke in the Port of Subic, as well as prior studies on the same issue that they
had read, prompted the researchers to conduct this study. Issues concerning
import/export documentation, frequent changes in customs procedures, and
slow computer systems were discovered. To help future customs brokers
prepare for issues outlined in the survey, the researchers then want to identify
and provide solutions for the issues they discovered.
It would be tremendously helpful to have a foundation on the problems that
customs brokers in the Port of Subic encounter, as well as the coping strategies
they employ to cope with them, as BS Customs Administration students who
aim to become licensed customs brokers. Knowing the challenges, they face
would help them foresee issues and prevent them from occurring, as well as lay
the groundwork for developing workable solutions for more effective service
delivery.
2. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
2.1 Research Design
The researchers used a mixed-methods research design. This approach aims
to integrate and blend qualitative and quantitative research approaches.
According to the Dovetail Editorial Team (2023), there are four different forms
of mixed-methods research design: convergent parallel, embedding,
explanatory sequential, and exploratory sequential. When analyzing the data in
this instance, the researchers employed the sequential explanatory design to
better explain the outcome. Lib Guides (2023), stated in their article that a
sequential explanatory design is a two-phase process that involves collecting
and analyzing quantitative data first, followed by collecting and analyzing
qualitative data based on the quantitative results. Additionally, they added that
the quantitative data is explained using the qualitative data. On the other hand,
the descriptive correlational research approach is used to explain the variables
and the correlations that naturally exist between and among them. It is used in
studies that display static representations of events and look for connections
between many parameters (Ivypanda, 2019).
To determine the challenges encountered by customs broker and their
coping techniques, the researchers used a variety of different research
methodologies. To better explain the quantitative and qualitative data, as well
as to find the connection between the two variables.
2.2 Treatment of Data
The data collected via Google form and hard copy were tallied and polished
using Microsoft Excel (2019) and then processed using statistical package for
social sciences (IBM-SPSS v.20). The following procedure were used:

71 | Pa ge
1. Percentage Frequency Distribution –used to determine the respondents’
profile in terms of age, sex, length of employment, nature of employment and
number of years transacting in the port of Subic.
2. Test of Normality – used to figure out whether the data had a normal
distribution or not in this instance, the researchers utilized the Shapiro-Wilk
test.
3. Weighted Mean – used to determine the difference of scope of practice and
challenges encountered as well as the coping strategies employed.
4. Pearson Product Moment of Correlation (Pearson - r) - used to examine the
link between the challenges experienced and the customs broker's coping
strategies.

Table 2 displays the challenges experienced by customs brokers. The overall
mean of 2.03 suggests that the obstacles were sometimes faced.
According to the findings, the most common challenges encountered by
customs brokers in their field of work were slow computer systems and
computer system breakdown. Both are rated as sometimes experienced, with a
total weighted mean score of 2.42. The e2m system in the Philippines has
experienced a computer slowdown due to processing numerous transactions
simultaneously, possibly due to the large number of users connected to the
internet provider.
According to Team T (2015), the computer program was improperly
designed and implemented, with no parallel or backup system. Customs brokers
in the Philippines have identified issues with the Terminal Appointment
Booking System (TABS), such as difficulty booking appointments due to a slow
computer system and unreliable internet connection. They also expressed
dissatisfaction with the inability to reach port operators via the contact

73 | Pa ge
information provided on the TABS website and the lack of documentation to
exempt trucks from TABS appointments.
As stated by Villotas (2014), customs forwarders and brokers have been
experiencing significant difficulties in clearing goods at customs, resulting in
significant losses for both importers and exporters. Most shipping lines and
forwarders have experienced issues with the recent e2m's implementation due
to system failures.
On the other hand, a computer system breakdown might be brought on by
dense data entry. The computer system might malfunction due to the volume of
encoded data. With regard to imports, several brokerage businesses had
problems, such as server failure when filing paperwork and problems with
confusing information stated. Their research demonstrates that these issues are
prevalent in businesses that engage in import-export operations. This results
from inadequate planning before system adoption (Cuevas et al., 2018).

achieving the desired goal, but it may also refer to the process of getting ready
for a strong launch toward a more desirable goal. According to Edison (2015),
a lot of unsuccessful individuals in life were on the verge of success when they
gave up.

Part II: Qualitative findings of the study
Theme 1: Appropriate traits and professional character
The characteristics and personalities of individuals are subject to
variation based on their environment and the individuals with whom they
interact. In the presence of friends and family, an individual's behavior may be
inappropriate, peculiar, or humorous without consequence. However, in a
professional setting, an individual must exhibit only professionalism and
meritocracy to earn the respect and trust of their colleagues. The impact of
professionalism in the workplace is significant, as it not only enhances an
individual's performance but also that of their colleagues. Professionalism
fosters positivity and confidence, while also providing opportunities for skill
development, which can contribute to a successful career.
 Sub-theme: Learning from Mistakes
Regardless of an individual's professional status, it is inevitable that
mistakes will be made, as it is an inherent aspect of human life. A mistake is
defined as an incorrect action or decision caused by misunderstanding or
ignorance, which typically results in adverse consequences. Nevertheless,
mistakes can prove advantageous if individuals acknowledge and learn from
them. Furthermore, mistakes can serve as a valuable instrument for exploring
beyond our comfort zones, acquiring knowledge, attaining experience or even
just for personal development.
Theme 2: Essence of seeking advice
The essence of seeking advice lies in the recognition that no individual
possesses all the knowledge, experience, and perspective necessary to make the
best decisions in every situation. We seek advice from others or people who can
help us be more optimistic and think smarter to solve our problem, broaden our
thinking, or acquire a different perspective on our circumstances, which will
influence our decision-making. Additionally, seeking advice is vital because it

79 | Pa ge
enables us to venture outside of our comfort zones, view situations from a new
angle, and form more accurate judgments.
 Sub-theme: Essence of seeking assistance
In a society that frequently promotes self-sufficiency and independence,
the essence of seeking assistance is often neglected. Recognizing our limits and
embracing the potential of cooperation, we may seek assistance to tap into the
skills, knowledge, and resources of others to achieve our goals more effectively
and efficiently. It also entails that, by seeking assistance from others, no one
can do it all on their own. And by seeking assistance from others, we build our
thinking, which creates a drive to study and achieve more.
Theme 3: Proper execution of port protocol & process
Proper execution is critical to success, it is major factor to effectively
implement strategies, plans, policies and etcetera. The Protocol and Process are
an essential part of every organization, this aims to provide a framework that
guides people whether professional or not on how to perform certain tasks
effectively and efficiently in their certain fields. A well performed one will
result to a better-quality service, safer work place and a well organize system.
 Sub-theme: Preparation, process and procedures
Planning ahead make’s different events and situations run smoothly, well
organize and effectively. Having procedures and process to follow through is a
big factor just to make the flow of the organization outstanding and better.
Regardless of profession and different fields this approach helps all people to
enhance the quality of products and services as well as improve the reputation
of them or its organization.
Theme 4: Coping by problem solving
Coping strategies are strategies that are used in order to deal with
problems or stressful situations. Everyone is vulnerable to stress especially
those who are working. By approaching problems with a systematic and logical
mindset, problem-solving allows individuals to break down complex issues into
manageable parts and develop strategies to overcome them. This approach
promotes critical thinking, decision-making, and resilience, enabling
individuals to adapt and find solutions to various life challenges.
 Sub-theme: Personal reflection and coping mechanism
Personal reflection and coping mechanisms are both important in
overcoming challenges. Personal reflection helps to recognize one’s actions and
to better understand ourselves and our behaviors in a certain situation which
will serve as our self-awareness. While coping mechanism is a strategy
employed in order to overcome difficulties that are faced in a specific situation.

80 | Pa ge
INTEGRATION OF QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE FINDINGS
AND RESULTS
Figure 1. Emerging Conceptual Framework
Figure 1 reveals that customs brokers face various challenges, including
computer system failures and complexities in accomplishing crucial customs
forms. These difficulties not only affect clients but also the brokers themselves,
leading to delays in paperwork and transactions, and ungracious demands from
customers. This can challenge the professionalism of customs brokers.
Two significant challenges have been identified in order to substantiate the
quantitative findings of the study's narrative inquiry and thematic analysis. The
first problem revolves around possessing the appropriate traits and exhibiting a
professional demeanor. Customs brokers may encounter difficulties in
maintaining a professional attitude and demonstrating suitable attributes when
faced with obstacles such as delays, missing documentation, and demanding
clients. However, it is imperative that they effectively address these challenges
while upholding their professional image. By doing so, they can adeptly
overcome obstacles without conflict and prevent any substantial damage to their
career.
The second problem revolves around the proper execution of the Port
protocol and process. Most customs brokers find it difficult to follow the port
protocol and procedures. This difficulty may arise not only because the customs
broker is required to follow it, but also because other parties such as clients,
logistic partners, and other entities conducting indirect transactions with the
Bureau are also expected to adhere to the protocol. Failure to follow the
procedure and adhere to the port protocol by these parties may cause
inconvenience not only for the customs broker but also for the flow of the
transaction.

81 | Pa ge
Protocols play a crucial role in various domains of society, such as science,
technology, data communication, and business. Adhering to protocols and
procedures is imperative to ensure accurate task execution. According to Power
DMS (2020), employees who follow procedures and protocols perform tasks
correctly and provide consistent service to clients and customers. Additionally,
adhering to protocols and procedures not only enhances individuals' knowledge
and skills but also helps them build pride and a good reputation.
In addition to the previous challenge of adhering to port protocols and
procedures, issues pertaining to document preparation, processing, and customs
transaction procedures were identified as a challenge. A crucial duty of a
customs broker is to meticulously prepare and process the requisite documents
for business transactions with the bureau. However, for a customs broker to
effectively carry out this task, the client must initially furnish all the essential
information and documents.
According to Pregmon et al. (2023), effective document management and
control practices can significantly decrease the time and resources needed for
document preparation, while simultaneously preventing any potential issues
that may arise during the process. As stated by Cooks-Campbell (2022),
individuals should establish comprehensive plans to ensure proper document
preparation and contingency plans to address any unforeseen complications and
minimize the resulting inconvenience.
In terms of coping strategies, customs brokers seek assistance from fellow
customs brokers, particularly those who have been in the profession for many
years. Senior practitioners have more experience in the field and are expected
to have gained more and deeper knowledge about why challenges in the field
occur and how to solve and conquer these challenges.
Consulting with experienced individuals is a beneficial practice as it
provides a straightforward approach to acquiring knowledge and assists in
developing solutions to problems. Seeking advice from others allows
individuals to receive guidance and ideas simultaneously, which is akin to
accomplishing two tasks at once. Additionally, seeking assistance from people
they know opens up the possibility of receiving fresh ideas or a new perspective.
Based on the quantitative results, problem-solving was found to be a
valuable coping mechanism for customs brokers. This approach not only
addresses the problem at hand but also facilitates the development of optimal
solutions, as stated by the South Calgary Primary Care Network (2020). When
employed correctly, a problem-solving approach grants individuals a greater
sense of control and predictability over their problems.
Coping with personal reflection falls under the purview of this coping
strategy. Engaging in reflection enables individuals to enhance their
comprehension of the underlying factors contributing to a particular situation.
As stated by Herbert-Smith (2023), self-reflection empowers individuals to
move beyond mere experience and towards understanding. Moreover, personal
reflection fosters self-awareness and mindfulness regarding one's actions,
enabling the identification of areas for growth and areas of proficiency.

82 | Pa ge
CONCLUSIONS
Based on the findings generated from this study, the researchers made the
following conclusions:
1. The respondents are mostly male, with ages ranging from 30-39 years old
and most of them are serving in the industry for 1-5 years. Also, almost entirely
of the respondents are from the private sector. Furthermore, the majority of the
respondents have been transacting in the port of Subic mostly for 1-5 years as
well.
2. Based on the result, the most frequent challenges encountered by the customs
broker in the Port of Subic were (1) Slow computer systems, (2) Computer
system breakdown, and (3) Lack of material time to meet the import/export
commitments. While on the other hand, the least challenge encountered was
inadequate working facilities. Moreover, other challenges were stated by the
respondents with which difficulties in completing required documents are listed
as the most frequent.
3. In the matter of coping strategies, the (1) customs broker seeks assistance
from fellow customs broker, and (2) When a customs broker encounters a
challenge at work, he or she does not give up easily; instead, he/she continues
to try to solve it were generally used by the respondents based on the outcome
of the results. Additionally, the customs broker tried to forget the bad things
that happened as a result of the work challenges he/she faced and carried on as
if nothing had happened was the most uncommon coping strategy used by the
respondents. Furthermore, the other coping strategies indexed by the
respondents were (1) The customs broker communicates with other customs
brokers or processors to seek advice or help, and (2) The customs broker is
completing and preparing documents on time or ahead of schedule which are
the most prevalent.
4. According to the findings, the researchers conclude that there is a weak
positive correlation between the challenges encountered and coping strategies.
According to thematic analysis, two major challenges were identified:
executing appropriate traits and professional character and adhering to port
protocol and procedure. In terms of coping strategies, two major things were
discovered: coping through problem solving and seeking advice.
RECOMMENDATIONS
Following a thorough examination of the study’s findings and conclusions,
the following recommendations are presented:
1. The study's findings were limited to customs brokers working in the Port of
Subic. It is recommended that the research not be limited to respondents from
one or two ports; if feasible, all ports in the Philippines should be covered. This
aims to collect data from customs brokers in various ports around the
Philippines, as well as to examine the disparities in the degree of challenges
they face, as well as the coping techniques they adopt based on the
location/ports where they practice customs brokerage.
2. It is recommended that licensed customs brokers engage in CPD, or
Continuing Professional Development, especially if they have worked in the
field for five years or more. This will help them greatly in reviewing and
updating their professional knowledge and skills that they can use to keep up
with changes in the customs brokerage industry.

83 | Pa ge
3. It is recommended that seminars should be held for both regular and new
importers/clients. This is to help them better understand the system and
processes involved in the import-export trade industry.
4. The researchers also recommend improving internet quality and computer
system by updating and upgrading their tools and system for technological
advancement in accordance with the Bureau of Customs objective of
computerizing and modernizing manual processes supporting Electronic to
Mobile System and shall focus through ICT related activities.
5. It is recommended that future researcher re-study the same topic from the
same place to see whether there has been development in the mechanisms
implemented in the import-export trading industry and the performance of
licensed customs brokers. In addition, the same research should be conducted
from the standpoint of freight forwarding and customs brokerage businesses.

SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH COMPETENCIES OF GORDON COLLEGE
FACULTY AND STAFF: BASIS FOR THREE-YEAR STRATEGIC
ACTION PLAN
Darwin P. Paguio1, PhD
Kristin Joy A. Mendoza2, MM-PM
1College of Education, Arts, and Sciences
2Human Resource Management Unit
ABSTRACT
This study determined the scientific research competencies of Gordon College personnel.
It utilized a descriptive design with the questionnaire as the main data-gathering tool.
Fifty-eight (58) personnel participated in the study selected through convenience
sampling. The research skills of respondents were measured through information-
seeking skills and methodology skills. The attitude of respondents toward research was
determined through eight dimensions using the Educators’ Attitudes Toward Educational
Research Scale. The research profile of the respondents reveals that they have very little
exposure to research-related training, seminars and conferences, and research
presentations at the institutional level and more so at regional, national, and international
levels. Faculty and staff who were able to attend have only attended one or two of these
activities. Research undertakings and publications were also minimal. Respondents
strongly agreed that they possess the skill of finding strategies to look for information and
that they are highly equipped with collecting survey data and conducting literature
reviews; however, they are weak when it comes to preparing a manuscript for publication
and writing an abstract. Respondents expressed strong agreement to valuing training in
educational research and believed that those who keep up with research are better
educators. On the other hand, they disagree that research findings are applicable in real-
life contexts.
Keywords: Scientific Research, Competencies, Local Higher Education Institution,
Gordon College
How to cite: Paguio, D.P., & Mendoza, K.J.A. (2022). Scientific research competencies of Gordon College
faculty and staff: Basis for three-year strategic action plan. The APO, 5(1), 61-76.
https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.10797478
INTRODUCTION
Research paves the way for development. The UNESCO World Declaration on Higher
Education for the Twenty-first Century (UNESCO, 1998) acknowledges that knowledge
creation, transmission, and application are the lifeblood of the knowledge-based
economy. Higher education institutions are among the primary entities tasked to
61

THE APO
Volume 1, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
generate, transmit, disseminate, and apply knowledge (CHED, 2009). This emphasizes
the integral role that higher education institutions play in research and innovation in the
country.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution in Article XIV, Section 10 mandates the prioritization of
research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization. Commission on
Higher Education, the country’s government agency that oversees higher education, is
mandated to promote, direct, and support higher education institutions in performing their
research and instruction functions. In pursuit of this, CHED in partnership with other
institutions and agencies developed the National Higher Education Research Agenda
which sets the policies, directions, priorities, and thrusts of Philippine higher education
research both long-term and medium-term.
Research, in addition to instruction and extension, has been identified as one of the
trifocal functions of HEI. As such, HEIs particularly universities are expected to lead in the
conduct of discipline-based, policy-oriented, technology-directed and innovative/creative
researches that are locally responsive and global (CHED, 2009).
Research is also one of the key areas in accreditation, and it is often called the “waterloo”
of most HEIs. This fact is manifested in several studies. For one, Bernardo (2003) in his
study on the typology of HEIs in the Philippines concluded that the majority of the HEIs in
the Philippines are teaching institutions. Results of his study showed that only 15 out of
223 HEIs in the sample met the requirements for the graduate-capable HEI category, and
only two HEIs met the criteria for doctoral/research university categories. Salazar-
Clemeña (2006) asserted that despite the initiatives of CHED, the Philippines’ current
state in terms of higher education research “leaves much to be desired in terms of
quantity, quality, thrusts, and contribution to national development”.
An assessment using bibliometric indicators of research productivity in the fields of
education and psychology in the Philippines by Vinluan (2012) revealed that when
benchmarked against the research productivity of Southeast Asian higher education
institutions in the same fields, the Philippines starting in the 1990s ranked low in research
productivity compared to countries such as Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia.
Specifically, the study elaborated that “only a few researchers, mainly coming from a
small number of higher education institutions were publishing papers on a regular basis
in a small range of journals”. In addition, the journals where the research was published
are described as having no or low impact, and the published papers had low citation
counts. In terms of collaboration, the study revealed that there is less collaboration with
institutions at the domestic and international levels. In explaining the low research
productivity, the paper identified several factors including economic factors, funding, the
local orientation of social science research studies, individual characteristics of
researchers, and the epistemic culture of knowledge production in the country.
Vinluan’s study attests to the claims, through the years, that only a few faculty members
in the higher education institutions in the Philippines conduct research and even few are
those who publish (Nuqui & Cruz, 2012; Salazar-Clemeña, 2006; Salazar-Clemeña &
Almonte-Acosta, 2007; Wa-Mbaleka, 2015).
Research looking at the factors that lead to low research productivity would show that
lack of training, lack of research skills, and even funding are the most prevalent reasons.
62

THE APO
Volume 1, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
Calma (2011), in a three-year study of research training policy and practice, participated
in by 53 government and university executives, and university academics in the
Philippines had several conclusions as follows: (1) there are inadequate facilities and
resources dedicated to support staff and student research; (2) there is a lack of specific
training to develop staff for research and supervision; (3) the emphasis of supervision is
on proofreading and the rewards are unattractive; (4) the range of student support
available is less dedicated to research; (5) there is low research quality in both staff and
student research; and (6) there is limited research collaboration locally and internationally
A follow-up study by Calma (2014) on the challenges in preparing academic staff for
research training and supervision showed that the most critical challenge faced by
academic staff in the Philippines is the challenge of effectively meeting the dual demands
of teaching and research. The other two challenges identified are building a critical mass
of researchers, and developing excellent research skills among staff and students.
An analysis by Quimbo and Sulaho (2014) of the research productivity of selected higher
education institutions showed that educational attainment, research benefits, and
incentive systems are important predictors of both research self-efficacy and research
productivity. Self-efficacy has also been found to be a significant determinant of
productivity. To promote research culture in higher education institutions, the study
suggested that a strong faculty development program, enhanced research collaboration,
improved research productivity, and a good incentive system. Five state universities in
the Philippines participated in this study, and a total of 377 randomly selected faculty
members served as research participants.
The Philippines, next to China, has the second largest number of public higher education
institutions (UNESCO Institute for Statistics, 2014, as cited in Wa-mbaleka, 2015) Public
HEIs consist of state colleges and universities which are funded by the national
government and local colleges and universities which operates under local government
units. While there are limited research undertakings and publications from faculty
members from SUCs and private HEIs, there are even fewer from faculty members from
LUCs.
This study was undertaken in one of the local colleges in Region 3, Gordon College, which
operates under the local government unit of Olongapo City. As a higher education
institution, it is mandated to ensure that it provides an academic environment that nurtures
and supports the research talents of faculty and staff. This paper was conceptualized to
determine the scientific research competencies of faculty and staff in this local college. It
aims to identify the areas where interventions may be put in place in order to strengthen
further the culture of research in the institution. Specifically, the study answers questions
on the research skills of faculty and staff in terms of information-seeking and methodology
skills. It also answers the question on their attitude towards research measured in terms
of specific dimensions. The results of the study served as the basis for the formulation of
a Three-Year Strategic Action Plan
Conceptual Framework
Utilizing the input-process-output model, the study used the profile of faculty and staff, as
well as their research skills and attitude towards research, as input. The profile included
63

THE APO
Volume 1, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
age, position, highest educational attainment, and number of years in service. Also
included as input are research skills measured vis-à-vis information-seeking skills and
research methodology skills.
In the study of (Meerah et al., 2012) aimed at developing an instrument to measure
research skills, five constructs were identified as necessary skills to conduct research.
These include statistical/quantitative analysis skills, information-seeking skills, problem-
solving skills, communication skills, and research methodology skills. Research skills, in
this study, were delimited to only two constructs, and their operational definition was also
adopted from Meerah et.al. Information-seeking skill is the awareness of various sources
of information that are available. It is the ability to search, use, and evaluate information.
On the other hand, research methodology skills involve identifying and designing
appropriate research procedures, and understanding the limitations and scope of
research design (for example, sample sizes and data type).
Another factor included under profile is the attitude of the personnel towards research.
The Educators’ Attitude Toward Educational Research Scale by Ozturk (2011) was used
to determine the attitude of the personnel. This scale was intended to provide reliable
and valid measurement of different aspects of educators’ attitudes toward educational
research (Ozturk, 2011).
The process frame included the data-gathering tool which is the questionnaire. Personal
and research profile were processed to obtain frequencies and percentages. Data on
research skills and attitudes towards research were analyzed through weighted mean. As
an output of the study, a Three-Year Action Plan to address the needs identified in the
study was put forth.
RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
Research Design
The study utilized a quantitative research design, specifically, a cross-sectional
descriptive design to determine the research skills and attitudes of faculty and staff.
Respondents of the Study
Respondents were selected through convenience sampling whereby data was collected
from the most readily, and conveniently available faculty and staff as samples for the
study. A total of 58 individuals voluntarily participated in the survey.
Instrumentation
Data was gathered through a three-part survey questionnaire. Part I gathered the
personal and research profiles of respondents. Part II pertained to the research skills
while Part III pertained to the attitude of the faculty and staff towards research.
Statistical Analysis
In order to analyze the gathered data statistically, the study used Microsoft Excel to
tabulate, organize, and calculate the statistical treatment. The study used frequency and
percentage in order to analyze the data gathered and presented it in a tabular method.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Personal Profile of Respondents
Of the 58 respondents, 27 (46.6%) fall under the age range 20-29, 15 (25.9%) belong to
the age range 30-39, 9 (15.5%) are 40-49 and 4 (6.9%) are 60 and above. Of these
respondents, 37, or 84.7 % respondents who hold teaching positions while 21 or 9.8 hold
administrative positions. This shows a sample who are mostly in their 20’s and 30’s and
more than half of whom are faculty members.
In terms of educational attainment, the highest percentage of the respondents have a
Bachelor’s Degree with Master’s Units, i.e., 23 (39.7%), 18 (31.0%) have a master’s
degree, 14 (24.1) have a Bachelor’s degree while 2 (3.4%) are master’s degree with
doctoral units. Only 1 is a doctoral graduate representing 1.7%. Results show that a
higher percentage of the respondents have either bachelor’s degree or have enrolled in
a master’s degree program. In higher education institutions, a master’s degree is required
in order to teach.
In terms of years in service, the majority have served between 1-4 years, specifically, 30
respondents (51.7%) while 10 (17.2%) have served 5-8 years, 9 (15.5%) have served 9-
12 years, 7(12.1%) have served for 13-16 years while 2 (3.4%) have served 17 years and
above. This data corroborates the data on age since most are still young.

CONCLUSION
Based on the aforementioned results of the study, the researchers hereby conclude the
following:
1) For the profile of the respondents, there were more respondents that belongs to
the age group 20-29 years old, working in teaching positions, having bachelor’s
degree with masteral units, and 1- 4 years in work service.
2) In terms of attendance to research trainings and conferences, there were more
respondents that have yet to attend any research trainings and conferences. For
research paper presentations, almost majority of the respondents have not
presented any paper in either institutional, regional, national, or international
events. As for research paper publication and research undertakings, the study
also yielded the same scenario.
3) For the faculty and staff research skills, they strongly agreed on information
seeking skills of the respondents and have satisfactory methodology skills.
4) In the case of attitude of faculty and staff towards research, the respondents
strongly agreed on the following terms: Valuing Training in Educational Research
and Belief of Keeping up with Research to be Better Educators. On the other hand,
the respondents only agree on the following: Value Doing Research in their
Schools, Incorporating Doing their Own Research in their Practices, Educators
Believe that Research Reports are Understandable, Time and Resources to Make
74

THE APO
Volume 1, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
Use of Research Findings, and Invest Time and Effort in Learning About Research
Findings. However, only Research Findings Are Applicable to Real Life Context
got a disagree response from the faculty and staff.
RECOMMENDATIONS
From the results and conclusion of the study, the researchers provided the following
recommendations:
1) The institution should strengthen the promulgation of its research agenda in order
for faculty and staff to promote a culture of research productivity among
themselves.
2) The faculty and staff should get involved in research and make it a habit that if
there is a problem in their workplace, research is one way of finding a solution.
3) The institution with the help of the Research Development and Publication Unit
should spearhead timely research skills and training programs in order to motivate
faculty and staff in doing research.
4) The Research Development and Publication Unit should also offer assistance to
interested faculty and staff in doing their research papers by means of consultation
and meetings in order to improve their papers.
5) The institution shall provide the necessary incentive schemes in order to help
prospective faculty and staff researchers to promote their confidence in research
productivity.
6) As an output of the study, a Three-Year Action Plan to address the needs identified
in the study was put forth.

INTRODUCTION
Education underwent a transformative shift as the global landscape evolved, with
online teaching emerging as a pivotal response to the changing dynamics. The novel
coronavirus disease 2019 or Covid-19 pandemic outbreak has disrupted and changed
how we socialize, work, and learn (Fauci, Lane, & Redfield, 2020; Velavan & Meyer, 2020;
Brynjolfsson et al., 2020; Daniel, 2020; Haase, Cosco, Kervin, Riadi, & O'Connell, 2021;
Gonzalez et al., 2020). The Internet, a catalyst for communication revolution, reshaped
1

DYNAMIC EDUCATION: FOLIO OF TRANSDISCIPLINARY (DEFT) JOURNAL
The Official Research Journal of College of Education, Arts and Sciences
(CEAS) - Social Sciences and Philosophy Department
Volume 1, Number 1, 2024
traditional teaching methods. Since the pandemic began, much human activity has
transitioned online (Donthu & Gustafsson, 2020; Kramer & Kramer, 2020). The COVID-
19 pandemic accentuated this transformation, compelling educational institutions to
confront the dilemma of closing schools for public safety while ensuring continuous
learning. This abrupt shift sparked an unprecedented reliance on online education,
creating both challenges and opportunities that educators and students around the world
had to grapple with. Students faced difficulties and challenges adapting to the abrupt and
unplanned shift to online learning (Baticulon et al., 2021).
As online teaching gained prominence, educators, like Mr. Asih Nurani and Arnold
Chan, found themselves at the forefront of this paradigm shift. The abrupt transition to
online teaching has significantly intensified workloads for staff as they move teaching
content and materials into the online space and become adept in navigating requisite
software (Allen et al., 2020, p. 233). Mr. Nurani, an English teacher at Regina Pacis Bogor
Junior High School, Indonesia, vividly recounted his initial apprehension towards running
an online class. "I may have been a teacher for the last nine years, but I never once
imagined running an online class. I knew I had to find new ways to engage my students,"
he reflected. Mr. Nurani also felt a responsibility to assist other teachers, especially senior
ones unfamiliar with distance teaching tools. His proactive approach aimed at molding
potential leaders for society, creating optimistic and motivating future generations on both
local and global scales.
Challenges with e-learning include accessibility, affordability, flexibility, learning
pedagogy, life-long learning, and educational policy (Pokhrel and Chhetri, 2021).
Recognizing the need for innovative engagement, Mr. Nurani took the initiative to assist
fellow teachers, emphasizing the transformative power teachers hold in shaping lives. In
the Philippines, Arnold Chan, a politics teacher at Maximo Estrella Senior High School,
also shared his story during an online class. "I have been a public-school teacher for four
years now, and I have always found joy in teaching. However, when the pandemic hit the
Philippines and classes migrated online, I was worried about delivering quality education
remotely," Chan admitted. His journey involved becoming a student again, learning to use
online tools and design engaging learning materials through the Asian Institute of
Journalism and Communication.
"After attending a few training sessions, I am now confident that I can provide the
same quality education online as I could in face-to-face classes," Chan affirmed. Filipino
educators faced the challenge of upskilling and adapting to digital platforms, a testament
to their dedication to maintaining the nation's ideals and building a prosperous future for
the next generation. Most institutions of higher education have had to reconsider ways of
teaching and assessment (García-Peñalvo, Corell, Abella-Garcí).
These stories mirrored the global struggle to bridge the digital divide and adapt to
the demands of online education. Teachers' commitment to upskilling reflected a
collective effort to shape a 21st-century learning environment, acknowledging the pivotal
role they played in students' lives. The narratives underscored the profound impact of
2

Volume 1, Number 1, 2024
flexibility and adaptability in navigating unforeseen challenges. In this context, the study
aimed to delve into the nuanced experiences of teachers navigating the transition to
online instruction, shedding light on the advantages, disadvantages, and limitations. By
sharing these stories, educators contributed valuable insights that could inform
educational institutions grappling with the intricacies of sustaining online learning
processes amid evolving paradigms.
Statement of the Problem
This study aimed to identify the experiences and realizations of teaching in the new
normal specifically it would answer the following questions:
1) How did the teachers handle their classes in the new normal?
2) What experiences did they have in the new normal?
3) What are their realizations in teaching during the new normal?
METHODOLOGY
Research Design
The research employed a qualitative research design, incorporating participant
impressions, in-depth interviews (conducted face-to-face or over the phone), and focus
groups as methodological approaches. These qualitative methodologies were selected to
facilitate a comprehensive exploration of participant experiences and perceptions. Within
the realm of qualitative research, the methodologies employed share commonalities,
emphasizing flexibility and the preservation of rich meaning during data interpretation.
The overarching goal of the qualitative research was to gain insights into how individuals
experience the world, employing an unfolding model in a natural setting that allowed the
researcher to actively participate in and observe personal experiences (Creswell, 1994).
The research also adopted a descriptive research design approach, which involved
the collection, processing, explanation, and presentation of evidence related to the
investigated scenario or event. The term "educational effectiveness" was coined to
encapsulate a more concise meaning than terms like "better" or "quality" education. The
effectiveness of teachers emerged as a critical factor in this novel method of learning,
with Dr. Skourdoumbis (2017) asserting that teacher competence and efficacy are pivotal
for classroom teaching reform. The term "educational effectiveness" was adopted to
emphasize the significance of teacher education as a fundamental foundation for
improving student success in preparation for the economic complexities of the twenty-first
century. The researcher meticulously analyzed all encounters of participant teachers to
extract meaningful insights.
Furthermore, the research incorporated a phenomenological approach, aiming to
delve into the lived experiences and perspectives of participants. Phenomenology offers
3

DYNAMIC EDUCATION: FOLIO OF TRANSDISCIPLINARY (DEFT) JOURNAL
The Official Research Journal of College of Education, Arts and Sciences
(CEAS) - Social Sciences and Philosophy Department
Volume 1, Number 1, 2024
a framework for exploring the essence of human experiences, capturing the nuances and
meanings attached to those experiences. This approach allowed the research to uncover
the depth and richness of individual perceptions within the context of the study.
Additionally, the research employed thematic analysis as a method for evaluating
qualitative data. This approach is particularly well-suited for describing patterns, subjects,
concepts, and significant trends within a group of texts, such as interview transcripts. The
researcher systematically analyzed the data to identify recurring themes, providing a
structured and insightful interpretation of the qualitative findings.
Participants
This study focuses on teachers actively teaching at Gordon College, specifically
tertiary educators who are college and university professors. These professionals play a
vital role in imparting skills and experiences to students across various disciplines. The
selected respondents are professionals known for their strong communication skills,
creativity, adaptability, and passion for teaching in the new normal setting.
For the participants' anonymity, the researcher used aliases to interpret their
responses in this study formally. The following participants are current instructors of
Gordon College.
Figure 1 shows the profile of the selected participants of this study and their teaching
experiences at Gordon College. They are the ones who have enough knowledge to answer the
questions formulated in this study. The answers they gave supplies the information that the
researchers needed.
Research Instrument
The primary instrument for this research is the interview, aiming to uncover the
advantages, disadvantages, limitations, and the experiences of teachers in the new
normal setting. Interviews, being a cornerstone for qualitative researchers, facilitate active
4

interactions to derive contextually based insights and concepts (Knox et al., 2009). In this
study, semi-structured interviews will be employed, following Mathers et al.'s (2002)
approach, featuring open-ended questions to cover specific topic areas while allowing for
in-depth discussions.
Observation, another qualitative technique, involves researchers observing
participants' ongoing behavior in real-life situations. The level of researcher participation
varies based on the study's goals and the type of observation research conducted.
Virtual interviews will be recorded for transcription, serving as the primary data for
the study. Additionally, an open-ended questionnaire will be prepared to complement and
justify the content obtained from both virtual and face-to-face interviews. The researchers
will also actively engage in online teaching alongside selected respondents, providing an
immersive experience to gather valuable information.
